# Rounding and remainders

Rounding to an integral value in a chosen direction, and the floating-point remainder.

<h2 id="ceil"><code>Ceil</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Ceil(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Ceil(x: float32) -> float32
```

Rounds `x` toward positive infinity to an integral value.
A negative value between zero and negative one becomes `-0.0`. A NaN or infinity passes through unchanged.

| Overload                               | Summary                                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Ceil(x: float64) -> float64` | Rounds `x` toward positive infinity to an integral value.   |
| `pub func Ceil(x: float32) -> float32` | Rounds `x` toward positive infinity at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Ceil.rux#L12)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description           |
| ---- | --------------------- | --------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value to round upward |

**Returns**: the smallest integral value greater than or equal to `x`

<h2 id="floor"><code>Floor</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Floor(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Floor(x: float32) -> float32
```

Rounds `x` toward negative infinity to an integral value.
The sign of zero is preserved. A NaN or infinity passes through unchanged.

| Overload                                | Summary                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Floor(x: float64) -> float64` | Rounds `x` toward negative infinity to an integral value.   |
| `pub func Floor(x: float32) -> float32` | Rounds `x` toward negative infinity at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Floor.rux#L10)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description             |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value to round downward |

**Returns**: the largest integral value less than or equal to `x`

<h2 id="mod"><code>Mod</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Mod(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64
pub func Mod(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the floating-point remainder of `x / y`, with the sign of `x`.
The result is `x - n * y`, where `n` is `x / y` truncated toward zero. Its magnitude is less than `|y|`. A zero
divisor, an infinite dividend, or a NaN operand returns a NaN; an infinite divisor returns `x`. The significands are
reduced with integer long division so the intermediate product cannot discard the remainder.

| Overload                                          | Summary                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Mod(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64` | Computes the floating-point remainder of `x / y`, with the sign of `x`.                        |
| `pub func Mod(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32` | Computes the floating-point remainder of `x / y` at `float32` precision, with the sign of `x`. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Mod.rux#L14)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | dividend    |
| `y`  | `float64` / `float32` | divisor     |

**Returns**: the exact remainder, or a NaN when no remainder is defined

<h2 id="round"><code>Round</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Round(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Round(x: float32) -> float32
```

Rounds `x` to the nearest integral value, with halfway cases away from zero.
Thus `Round(2.5)` is `3.0` and `Round(-2.5)` is `-3.0`. The sign of zero is preserved, and a NaN or infinity passes
through unchanged. The fractional part is compared directly instead of adding one half, which avoids prematurely
rounding the largest representable value below `0.5` up to `1.0`.

| Overload                                | Summary                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Round(x: float64) -> float64` | Rounds `x` to the nearest integral value, with halfway cases away from zero.                        |
| `pub func Round(x: float32) -> float32` | Rounds `x` to the nearest integral value at `float32` precision, with halfway cases away from zero. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Round.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description    |
| ---- | --------------------- | -------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value to round |

**Returns**: the nearest integral value

<h2 id="rounding-mode"><code>RoundingMode</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum RoundingMode: int32 {
    TowardZero = 0,
    TowardNegative = 1,
    TowardPositive = 2,
    ToNearestTiesAway = 3,
    ToNearestTiesEven = 4
}
```

Which way a value that falls between two integers should go.
`Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Rounding.rux#L16)

**Cases**

| Name                | Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TowardZero`        | `0`   | Toward zero, discarding the fraction: [`Trunc`](/docs/api/math/rounding#trunc).                                                                                                                                 |
| `TowardNegative`    | `1`   | Downward, toward negative infinity: [`Floor`](/docs/api/math/rounding#floor).                                                                                                                                   |
| `TowardPositive`    | `2`   | Upward, toward positive infinity: [`Ceil`](/docs/api/math/rounding#ceil).                                                                                                                                       |
| `ToNearestTiesAway` | `3`   | To the nearest, with a halfway value going away from zero: [`Round`](/docs/api/math/rounding#round). What most people mean by rounding, and what school teaches.                                                |
| `ToNearestTiesEven` | `4`   | To the nearest, with a halfway value going to the even neighbour. IEEE 754's default, and the one that keeps a long run of roundings from drifting: ties away from zero rounds up half the time and down never. |

<h2 id="round-ties-to-even"><code>RoundTiesToEven</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RoundTiesToEven(value: float64) -> float64
pub func RoundTiesToEven(value: float32) -> float32
```

The nearest integer to `value`, with a halfway value going to the even neighbour.
`RoundTiesToEven(2.5)` is 2 and `RoundTiesToEven(3.5)` is 4, where [`Round`](/docs/api/math/rounding#round) gives 3 and 4. The sign of a zero is
preserved, and a NaN or infinity passes through unchanged.

| Overload                                              | Summary                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func RoundTiesToEven(value: float64) -> float64` | The nearest integer to `value`, with a halfway value going to the even neighbour.                 |
| `pub func RoundTiesToEven(value: float32) -> float32` | Rounds `value` to the nearest integral `float32`, with halfway cases going to the even neighbour. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Rounding.rux#L38)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description    |
| ------- | --------------------- | -------------- |
| `value` | `float64` / `float32` | value to round |

**Returns**: the nearest integral value, resolving halfway cases toward the even neighbour

<h2 id="round-to"><code>RoundTo</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RoundTo(value: float64, mode: RoundingMode) -> float64

```

Rounds `value` in the requested direction at `float32` precision.

| Overload                                                          | Summary                                                           |

| `pub func RoundTo(value: float64, mode: RoundingMode) -> float64` | `value` rounded to an integer in the named direction.             |
| `pub func RoundTo(value: float32, mode: RoundingMode) -> float32` | Rounds `value` in the requested direction at `float32` precision. |

| Name    | Type                  | Description                       |

**Returns**: the integral value selected by `mode`

<h2 id="to-integer-checked"><code>ToIntegerChecked&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ToIntegerChecked<T>(value: float64, sample: T, mode: RoundingMode, result: *var T) -> bool
```

`value` rounded in the named direction and converted to an integer, reporting whether it fits.
`sample` is read by value and only its type matters, exactly as `Core`'s `MaximumOf` reads one. Returns `true` when
the rounded value is not representable in the integer type — because it is a NaN, an infinity, or simply out of
range — and leaves `result` zero in that case. This is the only place a float becomes an integer, and it refuses
rather than saturating, because a caller who has not thought about the out-of-range case is better served by a flag
than by a plausible wrong number. `result` must be non-null and writable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Rounding.rux#L102)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description              |
| ---- | ------------------------ |
| `T`  | destination integer type |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type           | Description                                       |
| -------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`  | `float64`      | floating-point value to convert                   |
| `sample` | `T`            | value used only to select `T`                     |
| `mode`   | `RoundingMode` | rounding rule applied before conversion           |
| `result` | `*var T`       | receives the converted integer or zero on failure |

**Returns**: `true` when the rounded value is not representable as `T`

<h2 id="trunc"><code>Trunc</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Trunc(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Trunc(x: float32) -> float32
```

Rounds `x` toward zero to an integral value at `float32` precision.
The wide result is exactly representable at the input width, so narrowing it back to `float32` loses nothing.

| Overload                                | Summary                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Trunc(x: float64) -> float64` | Rounds `x` toward zero to an integral value.                        |
| `pub func Trunc(x: float32) -> float32` | Rounds `x` toward zero to an integral value at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Trunc.rux#L11)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description       |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value to truncate |

**Returns**: the integral part of `x`
